articles.title: Uterine aging linked to poorer pregnancy outcomes after 49 despite donor eggs
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study presented at ESHRE links maternal age 49 and older with lower live birth rates and higher miscarriage risk after donor-oocyte treatment. The findings suggest uterine aging may affect outcomes even when donor eggs are used.

articles.title: Survey suggests Europeans support state-funded fertility care and embryo research across 4 countries
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Europe-wide survey reported broad public support for fertility treatment funding and several areas of reproductive research. The findings also point to areas where public understanding and opinions are still developing.

articles.title: A child can drown in seconds. Doctors want more families to be prepared
articles.summary_3_sentences: Doctors are warning families about rising child drowning deaths in the United States. The article emphasizes preparedness and prevention because drowning can occur very quickly.

articles.title: Vellore cohort reveals India's growing double burden of malnutrition in school-age children
articles.summary_3_sentences: A longitudinal cohort in Vellore found persistent thinness alongside rising overweight and obesity among school-age children. Overweight and obesity nearly tripled between ages 7 and 9 in the studied group.

articles.title: New adenomyosis atlas reveals lesion-specific signals that may spare healthy uterine tissue
articles.summary_3_sentences: University of Liverpool researchers identified distinctive biological features within adenomyosis lesions. The atlas could support more targeted treatments that spare healthy uterine tissue.

articles.title: Molecules link lower weight babies and chronic diseases
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers investigated molecular links between being small for gestational age and later chronic disease risk. The work addresses why lower birth weight is associated with adult heart, lung and metabolic conditions.

articles.title: Why more male than female newborns may get the crucial vitamin K shot
articles.summary_3_sentences: Vitamin K shots prevent dangerous newborn bleeding. The article reports that circumcision-related bleeding prevention may help explain why male newborns receive the shot more often than female newborns.

articles.title: Why grandparents matter more than ever for children's mental health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A child psychologist argues that grandparents can support youth mental health through listening, encouragement and meaningful connection. The piece emphasizes emotional resilience rather than achievement pressure alone.

topic_groups.topic: Brain, Aging, Cognition and Mental Health

articles.title: Speaking another language could slow aging in the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research presented at FENS Forum 2026 suggests multilingual people may show markers of younger brain aging. The report focuses on brain connectivity, which often declines with age.

articles.title: Rehab program helps lift long COVID 'brain fog'
articles.summary_3_sentences: A rehabilitation program is reported to help people with long COVID who experience brain fog. The symptoms described include problems with memory, attention and quick thinking.

articles.title: Higher blood glucose levels linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Higher blood glucose levels were linked with faster apparent brain aging. The report notes that accelerated brain aging may relate to memory loss and cognitive decline risk.

articles.title: Memories of childhood trauma remain stable over time but change more often in children than adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature Mental Health study found traumatic memories of childhood maltreatment are usually stable over time. Reports made during childhood changed more often than reports made during adulthood.

articles.title: How do humans visually discriminate materials?
articles.summary_3_sentences: A psychophysical VR study examined how people use head movements and object manipulation to judge material properties. The work explores visual perception and active exploratory behavior.

articles.title: You can dream while you're awake. The boundary between wakefulness and sleep is a lot blurrier than you'd think
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Cell Reports study suggests dreaming and waking thought overlap more than commonly assumed. The work describes dreamlike experiences before sleep and planning-like cognition after drifting off.

articles.title: Zebrafish brains reveal alternate route for senses to the forebrain shared with mammals
articles.summary_3_sentences: Zebrafish brain research identified an alternate sensory route to the forebrain with parallels in mammals. The findings suggest conserved principles across vertebrate brain organization.

articles.title: Researcher investigates enthusiasm as a distinct psychological emotion
articles.summary_3_sentences: Doctoral research argues that enthusiasm is a distinct emotion. The work links enthusiasm with energy, action and social connection.

articles.title: Scientists may have finally found how Alzheimer's spreads through the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that a common brain protein may help move toxic tau packages from damaged neurons to healthy ones. Blocking this process is presented as a possible future strategy to slow Alzheimer's progression.

articles.title: Scientists discover why some brains resist Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study suggests some brains resist Alzheimer's by supporting survival of immature brain cells after damage. The findings may inform future approaches to memory protection.

articles.title: Drinking to cope with stress may permanently rewire your brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research links stress-related drinking when young with lasting brain changes and later vulnerability to renewed drinking. The report also describes brain damage markers associated with early dementia.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and brain health
articles.summary_3_sentences: In more than 2,000 older adults in Japan, lower blood vitamin C was associated with less gray matter and weaker connectivity in a cognitive network. The study is observational and does not prove supplementation benefits.

articles.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering an idea Freud had 130 years ago
articles.summary_3_sentences: A paper compares predictive-processing theories of the brain with older psychoanalytic ideas. It argues that modern neuroscience may be reframing concepts explored more than a century ago.

articles.title: They knew the pill was fake but their memory still improved
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults improved on memory, physical performance and stress measures after three weeks of placebo pills. Effects were reported even when participants knew the pills were inactive.

articles.title: Brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patients under general anesthesia showed neural signs of sophisticated language processing while listening to stories. The findings challenge simple assumptions about unconsciousness but do not show conscious awareness.

articles.title: Scientists discover ancient brain cells that help block distractions
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified neurons in an ancient brain region that help filter distractions in mice. Temporarily disabling them made mice more distractible, with focus returning after reactivation.

articles.title: A surprising brain discovery is forcing scientists to rethink movement disorders
articles.summary_3_sentences: A cerebellum study found that two key cell types do not always behave in the expected linked pattern. The finding may affect how researchers interpret signals in movement disorders such as tremor and ataxia.

articles.title: This common vitamin deficiency can mimic normal aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes how vitamin B12 deficiency can cause fatigue and brain fog that resemble aging. It also notes research linking B12 to mitochondrial function.

articles.title: The real cause of a common stroke may have been missed for decades
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research suggests a common stroke subtype may be more strongly linked to damaged deep brain blood vessels than to fatty arterial plaque. The finding may help explain limited benefits from some standard treatments.

articles.title: Millions take omega-3 fish oil for brain health but a new study found no benefit
articles.summary_3_sentences: A two-year study found fish oil supplements delivered omega-3s to the brain but did not meaningfully improve cognition or Alzheimer's-related brain changes. The results question fish oil pills for cognitive prevention.

articles.title: Fish Oil Offers No Cognitive Benefit, Trial Finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: This report describes a trial in which fish oil supplements did not slow Alzheimer's-related brain changes or improve memory. The findings question cognitive benefits from fish oil supplementation.

articles.title: These fat-filled brain cells may be making multiple sclerosis worse
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found fat-loaded immune cells in severe multiple sclerosis brain tissue. These foamy cells may shift from repair roles toward inflammation and damage.

articles.title: Common pesticide linked to more than double the risk of Parkinson's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: UCLA researchers linked long-term residential exposure to chlorpyrifos with more than doubled Parkinson's disease risk. Laboratory work suggested damage to dopamine neurons and impaired toxic protein clearance.

articles.title: Tubulin prevents toxic brain protein clumps linked to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's
articles.summary_3_sentences: Baylor researchers report that tubulin can redirect tau and alpha-synuclein away from toxic clumping in brain cells. The work suggests a possible mechanism relevant to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: Yale study finds nearly half of older adults improved with age
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Yale longitudinal study found nearly half of adults over 65 improved physically, mentally or both over time. More positive views of aging were associated with these gains.

articles.title: Scientists discover neurons must break their DNA to build the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that migrating newborn neurons can experience double-strand DNA breaks while moving through tight spaces. The developing brain appears to repair this damage quickly.

articles.title: New brain study reveals speech learning works differently than we thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study suggests speech learning and memory depend strongly on sound and sensory processing, not only motor control areas. The findings may inform speech therapy and brain-based communication tools.

articles.title: Scientists reprogram brain immune cells to fight Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: A molecule called OLE restored more protective brain immune-cell activity in Alzheimer's models. The treatment reduced plaque buildup and improved memory in the reported models.

articles.title: Scientists discover how a single cell builds a brain with 170 billion cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose that brain-cell lineage helps organize neurons spatially during development. Cells from the same ancestor may remain near each other, acting as a positional map.

articles.title: Scientists May Have Found What Really Triggers Alzheimer's Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers suggest amyloid beta may trigger Alzheimer's by disrupting tau function rather than plaques alone being the root cause. The work reframes possible early disease mechanisms.

articles.title: 10 surprising ways diabetes and dementia are connected
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews links between diabetes and dementia through insulin, glucose, inflammation and vascular damage. It also notes research into whether diabetes medications may affect dementia risk.

articles.title: Higher Tyrosine in Men Linked to Shorter Lifespan
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study linked higher tyrosine levels with shorter lifespan in men. The report highlights questions about common supplement use.

articles.title: Copper drug clears toxic Alzheimer's proteins and restores memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: A copper-based compound reduced amyloid buildup and improved memory in laboratory experiments. The drug has reportedly been tested in humans for other neurological conditions, which may support further study.

articles.title: This popular brain supplement was linked to shorter lifespans in men
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large-scale study associated higher tyrosine levels in men with shorter lifespan. The article notes tyrosine is often marketed for focus and performance.

articles.title: Why middle age is becoming a breaking point in the U.S.
articles.summary_3_sentences: An international study found middle-aged Americans report more loneliness, depression and health problems than earlier generations. Researchers point to financial strain, weaker supports and chronic stress as possible contributors.

articles.title: Your brain can keep improving into your 90s, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A three-year study of nearly 4,000 adults found brain health measures can improve across adulthood into the 90s. Participants used brief daily brain-training activities.

articles.title: Learning a musical instrument in your 70s could help protect memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: A four-year study found older adults who kept practicing an instrument maintained memory and had less age-related brain shrinkage than those who stopped. Benefits were noted in memory-related regions.

articles.title: A hidden gene finally explains this rare neurological disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: Analysis of nearly 3,000 patients identified CD99L2 mutations as a genetic cause of a rare movement disorder. The gene was shown to have a role in nerve-cell communication.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising cancer link to Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers linked blood-cancer-associated mutations with inflammatory brain immune cells that may contribute to Alzheimer's disease. The finding could support blood-based screening or treatment ideas drawn from cancer medicine.

articles.title: Glucosamine Consumption is Linked to Increased Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Health-record analyses found an association between regular glucosamine use and higher dementia incidence. The study controlled for multiple confounders but remains observational.

articles.title: Over 600 New Genes are Linked to Schizophrenia
articles.summary_3_sentences: A genetic analysis identified more than 600 genes associated with schizophrenia. The findings highlight the disorder's complex and multifactorial biology.

articles.title: These Bits of Genetic Material can Help Control Rest Time
articles.summary_3_sentences: A zebrafish study found that neuronal microexons can influence rest-time regulation. Manipulating these small genetic segments altered sleep patterns in the model.

articles.title: Positive Attitude to Aging Linked to Better Cognition in Older Adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults with more positive attitudes toward aging were more likely to show cognitive and physical improvements. The report describes an association, not proof of causality.

articles.title: Popular joint supplement glucosamine linked to faster Alzheimer's progression
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major study associated glucosamine use with faster progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease. Researchers reported a 25% higher likelihood of dementia among users and explored possible biological explanations.

articles.title: Loneliness May Drive Mental Health Risks in Night Owls
articles.summary_3_sentences: People with an evening chronotype reportedly had poorer mental health, with loneliness suggested as a possible contributor. The article describes an association involving sleep timing and mental health.

articles.title: Ultra-processed foods may be stealing your focus even if you eat healthy
articles.summary_3_sentences: In more than 2,100 adults, higher ultra-processed food intake was linked to poorer attention and slower processing. The association persisted even among people with otherwise healthy diets.

articles.title: Scientists found a new Alzheimer's trigger and a drug that stops it
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a new Alzheimer's target and developed an experimental compound that blocked a damaging cellular process. In mice, it slowed nerve-cell loss and reduced Alzheimer's-related changes.

articles.title: Inflammation Worsens Brain Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses how inflammation can worsen brain damage after traumatic brain injury. It highlights immune responses as contributors to long-term cognitive effects.

articles.title: New targeted therapy shows promising early results in advanced pancreatic cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: An investigational targeted therapy combined with standard first-line chemotherapy showed promising early results in advanced pancreatic cancer. The therapy is designed to block a common genetic driver of the disease.

articles.title: A Founding Father Suffering from Facial Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses a historical figure affected by facial cancer in the context of the U.S. 250th anniversary. It uses the case to reflect on the personal impact of cancer.

articles.title: Common brain cancer mutation changes DNA shape to drive progression, exposing therapeutic target
articles.summary_3_sentences: MD Anderson researchers found that ATRX-mutant gliomas can rewire genome structure to support tumor progression. The study points to a possible therapeutic strategy for ATRX-mutant glioma.

articles.title: Forcing cancer cells to die can alert the immune system to enhance anti-tumor attack
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains how programmed cell-death pathways such as apoptosis and necroptosis may influence anti-tumor immunity. It discusses cell death as both a protective mechanism and a disease-related process.

articles.title: AI tool improves prediction of who will respond to cancer immunotherapy drugs
articles.summary_3_sentences: An AI tool was developed to improve prediction of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors. The goal is to better identify which cancer patients are most likely to benefit from these drugs.

articles.title: Are lung cancer tumors hijacking the nervous system?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses whether lung tumors may interact with the nervous system in ways related to cachexia. Cachexia causes unwanted muscle and fat loss and can limit cancer treatment options.

articles.title: New tumor map identifies high-risk B-cell lymphoma standard therapy may miss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers combined genetic and proteomic analyses to identify aggressive B-cell lymphoma features. The tumor map may help flag patients who need alternatives to standard therapy.

articles.title: Engineered Immunotherapy Improves Treatment for Brain Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports engineered immunotherapy research for brain cancer. Details are limited, but the focus is on improving treatment for aggressive brain tumors.

articles.title: A hidden weakness in deadly cancers could lead powerful new treatments
articles.summary_3_sentences: UCLA researchers found RB-deficient small cell cancers may depend on E2F3 for survival. Blocking E2F3 suppressed tumor growth in laboratory models, suggesting a possible treatment vulnerability.

articles.title: Melanoma's secret to cheating death has finally been revealed
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a genetic ingredient that helps melanoma cells become effectively immortal. The discovery may support treatments targeting cancer-cell survival mechanisms.

articles.title: FDA-approved drug may finally help immunotherapy defeat rare liver cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that rare liver cancer can divert T cells into nearby fibrous tissue. The FDA-approved drug AMD3100 freed T cells and improved immunotherapy effects in tumor samples.

articles.title: Chronic Stress-Induced Changes in the Gut Microbiome Impact Anti-Cancer Immunity
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article links chronic stress, gut microbiome changes and anti-cancer immunity. Details are limited, but it focuses on how prolonged stress may affect immune responses to tumors.

articles.title: Scientists discover an unexpected way to make pancreatic cancer cells self-destruct
articles.summary_3_sentences: Experimental PCAI compounds showed anticancer effects against pancreatic cancer cells. A leading compound blocked migration and hyperactivated signaling pathways until cancer cells self-destructed in laboratory work.

articles.title: New vitamin B12 therapy shows promise against deadly brain cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A vitamin B12-based compound crossed the blood-brain barrier and accumulated in glioblastoma tumors in animal studies. It delivered nitric oxide and enhanced existing glioblastoma treatments in preclinical models.

articles.title: A common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
articles.summary_3_sentences: A clinical trial is testing high-dose vitamin B3 in glioblastoma. Early results suggest niacin may help revive tumor-suppressed immune cells, but further confirmation is needed.

articles.title: Vitamin B12-Based Compound that Crosses the Blood-Brain Barrier May Serve as an Effective Brain Cancer Therapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a vitamin B12-based compound that can cross the blood-brain barrier and target glioblastoma. It presents the approach as a promising brain cancer therapy under investigation.

articles.title: USC scientists just unlocked an endless supply of cancer-fighting immune cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: A stem-cell-inspired method produced large numbers of immune-cell progenitors that can be engineered against cancer. In animal studies, the cells fought tumors and restored immune function.

articles.title: This DNA repair gene went rogue and exposed a cancer weakness
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that overproduction of the DNA repair gene EXO1 can create harmful DNA damage. The finding identifies a cancer-related vulnerability involving DNA repair machinery.

articles.title: Understanding the Switch From Benign to Malignant Tumors in NF1
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers studied molecular changes that drive neurofibromatosis type 1 tumors from benign to malignant states. The findings may point to therapeutic targets in NF1-related cancers.

articles.title: Cancer patients found a simple way to stay mentally sharp during chemotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a trial, cancer patients using a home exercise program had better attention and fewer noticeable chemotherapy-related cognitive problems. Low-dose ibuprofen improved some cognitive measures less consistently.

articles.title: New obesity figures highlight the income divide
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis of 55 million people found adult obesity in England rose from 26% in 2019 to 30% in 2025. The report emphasizes that obesity trends differ by income group.

articles.title: Five hidden pitfalls of fitness tracking
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews possible drawbacks of activity apps and wearables despite their usefulness for motivation and pattern tracking. It cautions that fitness tracking is not universally beneficial.

articles.title: Experts offer advice on performing endurance events in excessive heat
articles.summary_3_sentences: Experts offered guidance for endurance events during extreme heat in Western Europe. The article is framed around Tour de France preparations and heat-related health risks.

articles.title: Immature immune cells predict chances of survival following a heart attack
articles.summary_3_sentences: A University of Münster-led team found that neutrophil maturity after severe heart attack predicts short-term death risk. The biomarker may be measurable with a simple blood test.

articles.title: Creatine May Have Mental Health Benefits
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses possible mental health benefits of creatine beyond muscle performance. It notes proposed brain-energy mechanisms and the need for further study.

articles.title: HIIT Workouts Burn Fat and Preserve Muscle in Older Adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study reported that high-intensity interval training reduced fat while preserving muscle in older adults. The findings support HIIT as a possible body-composition strategy in aging populations.

articles.title: New calculator reveals whether you should really worry about statin side effects
articles.summary_3_sentences: Oxford scientists created a calculator to estimate individual risk of rare serious muscle disorders from statins. Their analysis found more than 98% of statin-eligible people were low risk, while many eligible patients were not taking statins.

articles.title: Scientists discover the deep sleep circuit that builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified brain circuitry linking deep sleep and growth hormone release. The feedback loop may help explain sleep effects on growth, metabolism, muscle repair and brain function.

articles.title: Scientists discover a protein switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that disabling a protein called Mitch in human cells increased fat burning and reduced new fat-cell development. Mice lacking Mitch were reported to be leaner and obesity-resistant.

articles.title: Scientists discover what triggers belly fat as we age
articles.summary_3_sentences: Aging was linked to specialized stem cells that increase belly fat formation. The discovery suggests a biological driver of middle-age weight gain and a potential treatment target.

articles.title: Researchers discover why fructose doesn't satisfy hunger like glucose
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, glucose more strongly suppressed hunger-promoting brain cells than fructose. The findings suggest sugar type may influence appetite and food preference beyond calorie content.

articles.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat without losing muscle
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-month study of adults in their 70s found HIIT reduced body fat while preserving lean muscle. Moderate and low-intensity exercise led to some fat loss but did not preserve muscle as well.

articles.title: Scientists say most people need more protein than current guidelines suggest
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review argues that more exercise and protein than minimum recommendations may help preserve strength, cognition and independence with age. The focus is healthspan rather than bodybuilding.

articles.title: A New Way to Lower High Cholesterol Levels is Found
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported a new method for lowering high cholesterol. The article frames the finding in relation to heart disease risk.

articles.title: The tea in your kombucha changes more than just the taste
articles.summary_3_sentences: Kombucha chemistry, flavor and antioxidant activity varied depending on the tea used. Green and oolong tea kombuchas were reported as especially biologically active.

articles.title: One common fat may fuel type 2 diabetes while another helps fight it
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers contrasted palmitic acid, which may promote insulin resistance through inflammation and stress, with oleic acid, which may protect insulin function. The work highlights different metabolic effects of dietary fats.

articles.title: Ozempic changed obesity treatment, but experts say the real revolution is next
articles.summary_3_sentences: Experts reviewed how GLP-1 drugs have changed obesity treatment. They anticipate future care combining medications, procedures, surgery and precision approaches.

articles.title: Butter and margarine look similar but their chemistry changes everything
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains how butter and margarine differ chemically despite similar appearance. Their fat structures affect flavor, browning, shelf life and culinary performance.

articles.title: Most people who stop GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic eventually return
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found many people with type 2 diabetes stop GLP-1 drugs but later restart treatment. Newer medications were associated with longer persistence, while side effects remained a common reason for stopping.

articles.title: Semaglutide (Ozempic) linked to fewer bone fractures despite greater weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: A real-world study of nearly 60,000 adults with type 2 diabetes linked semaglutide with about 15% fewer fractures than comparator weight-loss medications. The association occurred despite greater weight loss.

articles.title: Calcium and Vitamin D Don't Prevent Bone Fractures
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large clinical trial found calcium and vitamin D supplements did not reduce fracture or fall risk in older adults. The results challenge routine supplementation for fracture prevention in this context.

articles.title: New GLP-1 diabetes pill delivers major weight loss and blood sugar control
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major clinical trial found an oral GLP-1 drug improved blood sugar control and produced substantial weight loss in type 2 diabetes. The pill could offer a more convenient treatment option.

articles.title: People taking GLP-1 weight loss drugs like Ozempic started moving less
articles.summary_3_sentences: Fitbit data suggested people taking GLP-1 weight-loss drugs reduced steps and exercise after starting treatment. The article raises concerns about preserving muscle and long-term health during weight loss.

articles.title: More Protein Plus More Exercise Lengthens Healthspan
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that higher protein intake combined with more exercise may improve lifespan and healthspan. Details are limited, but the focus is aging-related strength and function.

articles.title: A new guideline links care for heart, kidney and metabolic diseases
articles.summary_3_sentences: A guideline treats heart disease, kidney disease, diabetes and obesity as connected under CKM syndrome. The approach aims to coordinate care across related cardiometabolic conditions.

articles.title: Sleep and exercise may dampen genetic drivers of heart disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mouse data suggest sleep and exercise may offset immune-cell mutations that promote atherosclerosis. The findings are preclinical and require human validation.

articles.title: 90-120 Minutes of Strength Training Per Week Increases Lifespan
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that 90 to 120 minutes of weekly resistance training may be associated with longer life. It highlights strength training as a practical health behavior.

articles.title: We can't entirely blame COVID vaccine mandates for lower vaccination rates today. It's not that simple
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article argues that declining childhood vaccination rates reflect many factors beyond COVID vaccine mandates. It cites hesitancy, political distrust, institutional distrust and disinformation.

articles.title: Decade-long national study finds antimicrobial use in Australian hospitals improves with regular monitoring
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 10-year Australian study found hospital antimicrobial prescribing improved when facilities regularly monitored use. The findings support antimicrobial stewardship to improve care and limit resistance.

articles.title: Early dog exposure may protect babies from infections through home microbes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early childhood dog contact was associated with fewer infections and antibiotic courses. The protective association may be partly explained by dog-associated microbes spreading through the home.

articles.title: Rare Immune Stem Cells Help Fight Inflammatory Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on rare immune stem cells involved in inflammatory disease. Details are limited, but the work focuses on T-cell biology and inflammation control.

articles.title: Scientists discover a completely different way to fight viruses
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified an unusual antiviral defense system in sea anemones. The discovery suggests animals evolved multiple immune strategies against viruses.

articles.title: Scientists discover hidden "footprints of death" that may help viruses spread
articles.summary_3_sentences: Dying cells leave microscopic packages that help guide immune cleanup. Researchers found influenza viruses may exploit these packages to spread to nearby cells.

articles.title: One tiny mutation may explain how bat viruses become human threats
articles.summary_3_sentences: A single amino-acid difference altered coronavirus behavior across species in a comparison of SARS-CoV-2 and a related bat virus. The finding may help explain zoonotic spillover risk.

articles.title: Ebola and hantavirus can start like the flu but turn deadly fast
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews hantavirus and Ebola as severe infections that may begin with flu-like symptoms. It notes limited hantavirus treatment options and improved tools for some Ebola strains.

articles.title: One of the world's most popular weedkillers may be fueling deadly superbugs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found highly drug-resistant hospital bacteria were also resistant to glyphosate. The discovery raises concern that herbicides could help antibiotic-resistant microbes survive outside health care settings.

articles.title: Scientists finally solved how H5N1 bird flu hid in dairy cows
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found H5N1 bird flu receptors concentrated in cow mammary tissue, explaining udder infections. The work may help identify unusual infections and predict future jumps.

articles.title: Johns Hopkins scientists develop nose spray DNA vaccine for tuberculosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: An intranasal DNA vaccine improved tuberculosis clearance, reduced lung inflammation and prevented relapse in animal studies. It also enhanced drugs used against resistant TB in the reported models.

articles.title: Ancient DNA reveals plague was already killing humans 5,500 years ago
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ancient DNA from Siberian hunter-gatherer cemeteries revealed early plague strains in many individuals. The findings suggest lethal family-based outbreaks long before historic urban plague conditions.

articles.title: Investigating Escherichia albertii – An Emerging Pathogen
articles.summary_3_sentences: Genomic sequencing of Escherichia albertii isolates identified virulence factors and transmission clues. The findings support improved detection and surveillance of this emerging foodborne pathogen.

articles.title: New fentanyl vaccine blocks deadly overdoses before they start
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scripps researchers developed an experimental vaccine designed to keep fentanyl and related designer drugs from reaching the brain. The vaccine trains the immune system against a broad range of fentanyl-like compounds.

articles.title: A new method could spot fentanyl variants no one has cataloged yet
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used machine learning to predict chemical signatures for more than 1 billion possible fentanyl variants. The method could help identify variants not yet cataloged.

articles.title: Proteins Help Deadly Pathogen Evade Immunity
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified bacterial proteins that help the louse-borne relapsing fever pathogen evade antibody binding. Understanding this immune evasion may aid treatment or vaccine design.

articles.title: DNA Regulation Drives Antibody Diversity
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses DNA regulatory mechanisms that help generate antibody diversity. It focuses on how immune cells produce varied immunoglobulins for pathogen recognition.

articles.title: Measles has no treatments. Changing that may not be easy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article notes that vaccination remains the main measles prevention tool because no approved treatments exist. Researchers are exploring drugs for people who are unvaccinated or infected.

articles.title: The deadly tapeworm spreading across America has reached the Pacific Northwest
articles.summary_3_sentences: Echinococcus multilocularis was detected in coyotes around Puget Sound, marking a West Coast wildlife finding. The parasite can cause severe cancer-like disease in humans.

articles.title: One Amino Acid Switch Can Move a Virus from Bats to Humans
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found a single amino-acid change can enable a bat virus to infect human cells. Structural analysis showed the mutation affects receptor binding, underscoring spillover risk.

topic_groups.topic: Substance Use, Cannabis, Pain and Behavioral Health

articles.title: Study Analyzes Legal Cannabis Packaging Features That Appeal to Youth
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Washington State University study examined legal cannabis packaging and identified design features attractive to younger consumers. The findings raise youth-marketing concerns.

articles.title: Cannabis Treatments for Parkinson's Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research evaluated medical cannabis in people with Parkinson's disease. It assessed symptom management and potential therapeutic benefit.

articles.title: Cannabis-Tobacco Co-Use Linked to Lower Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: Cannabis and tobacco co-use was linked to lower cognitive performance in people at high clinical risk. The report describes an association and cautions against combined use.

articles.title: Inhaled cannabis replaces opioids for back pain study
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study examined inhaled cannabis for back pain and whether it could reduce opioid reliance. The report presents cannabis as a potential pain-management alternative under investigation.

articles.title: Scientists say creatine may help fight depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review of five randomized trials found mixed evidence for creatine in depression. Two studies in women with major depressive disorder found benefit as add-on treatment, while three did not.

articles.title: Does Creatine Help with Depression?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports possible antidepressant effects of creatine supplementation. It notes that further investigation is needed to confirm benefits for major depressive disorder.

articles.title: Massive study links teen marijuana use to double the risk of serious mental illness
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 463,000 adolescents linked cannabis use with higher risk of later psychotic and bipolar disorders. Cannabis use often preceded diagnosis, but the report should not be read as definitive proof of causality.

articles.title: Study Explores the Safety and Tolerability of CBD and Alcohol Use
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Cannabis Research study assessed safety and tolerability when cannabidiol is combined with alcohol. The work examined adverse effects and interaction profiles.

articles.title: Scientists found a cannabis compound that relieves pain without the high
articles.summary_3_sentences: Cannabis-derived terpenes reduced pain in mouse models of fibromyalgia and post-surgical pain. Geraniol showed strong effects and is not associated with THC-like psychoactivity.

articles.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to surprising drop in violent behavior
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Rutgers study linked GLP-1 drug use with a weaker association between impulsivity and violent behavior. Researchers emphasized that causality has not been proven.

articles.title: Genetic Analysis of Cocaine Addiction Points to the Liver
articles.summary_3_sentences: A rat genetic analysis pointed to liver-related genes influencing cocaine addiction susceptibility. The findings suggest metabolic pathways may contribute to substance dependence.

articles.title: Study Found Teen Cannabis Use Interferes with the Brain's Reward System
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Neuropsychopharmacology study linked adolescent cannabis use with differences in the brain reward system. Details are limited, but the focus is cannabis exposure during development.

articles.title: Topical CBD Calms Acne Redness
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on topical CBD for acne redness and skin inflammation. Details are limited, but it frames CBD as a dermatologic anti-inflammatory candidate.

articles.title: Decriminalizing Cannabis Doesn't Increase Cannabis Use
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that cannabis decriminalization and tightly controlled legalization were not linked to increased use. Details are limited, but the focus is cannabis policy and consumption patterns.

articles.title: Probiotics May Complement Antidepressant Treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Daily probiotic supplementation may complement antidepressant treatment in older adults. The article provides limited details but highlights the gut-brain axis in depression care.

articles.title: World's largest opioid review finds they often don't work
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large review found opioids often provide only small, short-lived benefits for acute pain and sometimes no advantage over placebo. The review also reported more side effects and dependence concerns.

articles.title: 64% of Cannabis Consumers Say It Helps Them Sleep
articles.summary_3_sentences: A survey reported that 64% of cannabis consumers say cannabis helps them sleep. The article concerns self-reported sleep effects rather than objective sleep outcomes.

topic_groups.topic: Musculoskeletal, Regenerative Medicine and Medical Devices

articles.title: Genetic information helps predict the onset and progression of glaucoma
articles.summary_3_sentences: Genetic information improved prediction of glaucoma onset and progression. Earlier targeted screening could help detect disease before irreversible optic nerve damage.

articles.title: Australians missing out on 'major gap' between innovation and patient care
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Curtin University review found many Australian risk-prediction tools are not routinely used in health care. The gap affects tools for heart disease, falls, frailty and diabetes complications.

articles.title: This spray-on powder can stop life-threatening bleeding in 1 second
articles.summary_3_sentences: KAIST researchers developed a spray-on powder that forms a gel over wounds and stops severe bleeding rapidly. The material is designed for deep irregular injuries and harsh storage conditions.

articles.title: Osteopenia is silently weakening bones in millions of people
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains osteopenia, a common silent reduction in bone density that raises fracture risk. Exercise, calcium, vitamin D and healthy habits may help slow bone loss.

articles.title: Nearly half of kidney transplant patients never even get started
articles.summary_3_sentences: A national study found nearly half of referred U.S. kidney failure patients never begin transplant evaluation, and only 19% reach the waitlist. Geography, income, marital status, language, age and center factors affected progress.

articles.title: This emerging treatment is helping people avoid knee replacement surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: Genicular artery embolization is described as a minimally invasive treatment for chronic knee pain. Early studies suggest it may reduce joint inflammation and provide lasting relief for some patients.

articles.title: One injection reversed osteoarthritis in weeks
articles.summary_3_sentences: Colorado researchers reported experimental osteoarthritis injections that regenerated damaged joints in animal studies. The preclinical therapies appeared to restore arthritic joints and repair cartilage and bone defects.

articles.title: New procedure delivers lasting knee arthritis pain relief without surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: A minimally invasive knee procedure blocked inflammation-driving blood vessels and improved osteoarthritis pain and function for at least one year. The report presents it as an option before knee replacement.

articles.title: Stanford scientists regrow lost cartilage and reverse arthritis in major breakthrough
articles.summary_3_sentences: A treatment blocking an aging-related protein restored cartilage in old mice and helped prevent post-injury arthritis. Human cartilage samples showed similar regenerative signals, but the work remains early.

articles.title: A Novel Way to Deliver Drugs to the Esophagus
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed a platform to deliver drugs directly to the esophageal lining. Preclinical testing showed improved retention and therapeutic effect for esophageal disease models.

articles.title: Ancient Chinese medicine could transform hair loss treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research reviews Polygonum multiflorum, a traditional Chinese medicinal root, for potential hair-loss treatment mechanisms. Reported effects include hormone blocking, follicle protection and growth-signal activation.

topic_groups.topic: Basic Science, Genetics, Ecology and Technology

articles.title: Water mixing causes heavy metal spikes Texas neighborhood
articles.summary_3_sentences: An investigation found that mixing certain water sources caused heavy metal spikes in a Texas neighborhood. The findings raise environmental health concerns.

articles.title: These tiny soil microbes could rescue crops from salty farmland
articles.summary_3_sentences: Beneficial soil bacteria helped plants survive salty soils by stimulating lignin production in roots. Greenhouse and field tests showed healthier plants and higher yields under salty conditions.

articles.title: The secret to healthy aging may be hidden in your blood
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found centenarians have distinctive blood chemical patterns, including bile acid and steroid profiles. The signatures were linked with longer survival and healthy aging.

articles.title: Scientists stunned as bumble bees solve a classic intelligence test
articles.summary_3_sentences: Bumble bees devised a new way to reach a hidden reward without being taught. The study adds evidence for flexible problem-solving in insects.

articles.title: 5,000-year-old wolves found on remote island rewrite what we know about domestication
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ancient wolves on a Baltic island appear to have been brought there by humans. Evidence suggests close human-wolf relationships before modern domestication concepts.

articles.title: Quantum mechanics once baffled scientists. Now it's changing the world
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews quantum mechanics from its controversial origins to its role in modern technologies. It notes potential applications in energy, medicine, computing and physics.

articles.title: Why South Africa's leopards shrank to half their normal size
articles.summary_3_sentences: Genome analysis found Cape Floristic Region leopards are small and genetically distinct after long isolation. Despite small population size, they retained notable genetic diversity.

articles.title: The universe may be hiding conscious minds stranger than we can imagine
articles.summary_3_sentences: Philosophers argue consciousness may arise in non-Earth-like beings or materials elsewhere in the universe. The article presents a speculative argument rather than empirical evidence.

articles.title: Scientists just discovered how queen bees are really made
articles.summary_3_sentences: New research suggests queen bee development depends on specialized wax cribs, regulated humidity and temperature, and worker care. The findings complicate the traditional royal-jelly-only explanation.

articles.title: From pet to pest, goldfish can wreck entire ecosystems
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found released goldfish can cloud water, disrupt food webs and harm native fish. The work highlights ecological risks from pet releases.

articles.title: Butterfly that barely ages could help unlock longevity secrets
articles.summary_3_sentences: Heliconius butterflies live much longer than related species and show limited physical decline with age. Their pollen-feeding lifestyle and evolutionary changes may provide longevity clues.

articles.title: Long-lived families reveal a rare genetic clue to healthy aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of long-lived families identified rare genetic variants linked to healthier aging. One mutation may reduce inflammation and delay disease.

articles.title: Mountain lions changed everything in this tiny California preserve
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mountain lion presence in a small California preserve reduced deer activity and helped plants recover. The study shows trophic cascades can occur in suburban preserves.

articles.title: Hidden bird species discovered in Japan after DNA reveals a stunning secret
articles.summary_3_sentences: DNA and song analyses revealed a newly identified Tokara Leaf Warbler distinct from Ijima's Leaf Warbler. The discovery is Japan's first new bird species finding in more than 40 years.

articles.title: Think human anatomy is finished? Scientists say think again
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article notes that researchers continue finding overlooked human anatomical structures and individual variation. It argues anatomy remains less complete than textbooks imply.

articles.title: DNA time stamps reveal the strawberry's surprising origins
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used transposable-element traces to reconstruct complex plant genome history. The method showed modern strawberries arose through multiple ancient genome-merging events.

articles.title: Novel, Protein​-Chaperone Role for RNA is Revealed
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found RNA can act as a chaperone that helps proteins fold and stabilize. The discovery expands understanding of RNA functions beyond coding proteins.

articles.title: Scientists say most of what's in your food is still a mystery
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers describe thousands of poorly characterized food chemicals as nutritional dark matter. Understanding them may clarify diet effects on disease risk and aging.

articles.title: Scientists turned red lettuce green and something surprising happened
articles.summary_3_sentences: Genome editing blocked red pigment production in lettuce and caused other beneficial compounds to accumulate. The plants grew normally, suggesting a route to customized crop nutrition.

articles.title: Beneath our feet lies a fungal superhighway stretching 68 quadrillion miles
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers mapped vast underground fungal networks and estimated their global extent and carbon movement. The networks support plants and may influence climate regulation.

articles.title: Researchers Find a Cause of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a molecular pathway and genetic variants linked to intestinal inflammation in inflammatory bowel disease. The findings may guide targeted therapies.

articles.title: Millipedes beat vertebrates to land by 80 million years
articles.summary_3_sentences: A new millipede evolutionary tree suggests they colonized land nearly 460 million years ago. The work sheds light on early terrestrial ecosystems and chemical defenses.

articles.title: A popular sunscreen ingredient can finally be sold in the United States
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA will allow bemotrizinol in U.S. sunscreens. The ingredient is long-lasting and protects against solar radiation involved in skin aging.

articles.title: No, mastic gum won't reshape your jaw
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article says mastic gum may have mouth and gut benefits but will not reshape the jaw. It addresses a health claim circulating around chewing gum.

articles.title: A legendary golden fabric lost for 2,000 years has returned
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers recreated sea silk using clam fibers and found its golden shine comes from protein structures rather than pigments. The structural color can remain vibrant for centuries.

articles.title: Genetic Variants Cause IBD – Potential Treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study linked specific genetic variants with inflammatory bowel disease susceptibility. The report suggests the variants could inform personalized treatment development.

articles.title: A classic brain test exposed AI's biggest weakness
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers gave AI models a classic attention test and found performance collapsed as tasks became longer and more complex. The work highlights limitations in sustained attention-like processing.

articles.title: Scientists mapped every neural connection in a fruit fly and found a surprise
articles.summary_3_sentences: A complete adult fruit fly central nervous system connectome mapped neural connections across brain and body. The findings suggest behavior emerges from distributed local circuits.

articles.title: Scientists propose a radical new theory for how life began on Earth
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose mineral nanoparticles acted as catalytic and energy-processing nanozymes in early Earth chemistry. The theory aims to explain how lifeless matter produced life's building blocks.

articles.title: From Atlas to Action: Going Deeper in the Next Era of Spatial Biology
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses how spatial biology extends cell atlases by locating cells in their tissue context. These methods reveal cell interactions relevant to tissue organization and disease.

articles.title: Beyond the bead: rethinking small​-scale protein purification
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article evaluates limitations of bead-based small-scale protein purification. It describes a bead-free workflow intended to simplify handling and improve yield.
